title: Does a waste that remembers the trait DISTRIBUTION (random-feature channels) rather than its local mean remove the cloud-radius bound of the standard waste vortices, and does the long-memory travel speed follow Heyde-Mahadevan's eps^1/2-then-decline law in ew?
summary: c58's waste stores V/W, the local mean trait of past eaters, and holds back a vortex by exp(-|theta - V/W|^2/2sw^2); the standard-memory population then fills a cloud of radius ~2.5 sw and stops reaching new ground (20261028T0118-c61-vortex-t30k-interim). Replace V by K random-feature channels U_k (pw eat sqrt(2/K) cos(w_k.theta+b_k), w_k ~ N(0, I/sw^2), fixed draws) and use G = sum_k phi_k(theta) U_k / W, the mean Gaussian similarity to the eaters' trait distribution. Predictions: the cloud no longer stops at ~2.5 sw; with long memory the population travels and may branch (Heyde & Mahadevan 2026).
experiment: Copy 20261027T1401-c58-vortex-trait3d/world.py, add waste mode 'rff' with K=32 channels (check G against the exact kernel on a two-trait test first: error < 0.15), and run trait3c.py (20261028T0118-c61-vortex-t30k-interim) on 2 fresh seeds, T=10000, waste arm vs kind-blind twin, standard dw 0.002. Score with vnov.py (20261028T0105) for cloud radius, new-ground share and diversity-corrected c30 kinds. Separately, at long memory (dw 0.0005, Dw 0.25), run ew 0.1, 0.25, 0.5, 1.0 on one seed and report centroid speed per 1000 t.
